body: Millions of children grow up in places affected by conflict, where school, food and safety are never guaranteed.
全世界有数百万孩子在冲突地区长大，那里上学、吃饭和安全都无法得到保障。
Aid workers say the damage is not only physical: constant fear can affect a child's sleep, memory and learning for years.
救援人员说，伤害不只是身体上的：长期的恐惧会在之后很多年里影响孩子的睡眠、记忆和学习。
Simple things, such as a safe classroom or an adult who listens, help children recover more than people expect.
一些简单的事，比如一间安全的教室、一个愿意倾听的大人，对孩子恢复的帮助远超人们的想象。
For many families, dinner turns into a battle, with parents begging children to eat vegetables they clearly dislike.
对很多家庭来说，晚饭变成了一场拉锯战，父母不停求孩子吃他们明显不爱吃的蔬菜。
Experts suggest putting new food on the table without pressure, and letting children look at it, touch it, or simply ignore it.
专家建议把新食物放上桌但不施加压力，让孩子看看它、摸摸它，或者干脆无视它。
Over time, calm repeated exposure works far better than rewards or punishment, and mealtimes get quieter for everyone.
时间久了，平静地反复接触比奖励或惩罚有效得多，全家的饭点也会安静下来。

articles.zh: 该怎么管孩子的屏幕时间
body: Screens are now part of childhood, and many parents worry about how many hours their children spend scrolling.
屏幕已经成了童年的一部分，很多父母担心孩子每天要刷多少小时手机。
Researchers say the type of content matters as much as the total time; a video call with grandparents is not the same as endless short videos.
研究者说，内容类型和总时长一样重要：和爷爷奶奶视频通话，跟无休止地刷短视频完全是两回事。
Agreeing on clear rules together, like screen-free meals and no phones before bed, usually works better than a sudden ban.
一起商定清楚的规则，比如吃饭不看屏幕、睡前不碰手机，通常比突然全面禁止更管用。

articles.en: How Advertisers Make Us Spend Money
articles.zh: 广告是怎么让我们掏钱的
body: Advertisers study our habits carefully, then design messages that make us feel we are missing out on something.
广告商会仔细研究我们的习惯，然后设计出让我们觉得「再不买就错过了」的信息。
Limited offers, countdown timers and 'only three left' notices all push us to decide quickly, before we think.
限时优惠、倒计时和「仅剩三件」的提示，都在推着我们在思考之前赶紧下单。
Noticing the trick is the best defence: wait one day, and most must-have items quietly lose their power.
识破套路就是最好的防御：等上一天，大多数「非买不可」的东西会悄悄失去魔力。
Poetry can look difficult, but at heart it is simply language slowed down until we finally notice it.
诗看起来很难，但本质上不过是把语言放慢，慢到我们终于注意到它。
Studies suggest that reading or writing poems helps people name feelings they cannot easily explain.
研究表明，读诗或写诗能帮人给那些说不清的情绪起个名字。
You do not need talent to begin: three honest lines about your day already count as a poem.
开始写诗并不需要天赋：关于今天的三句真心话，就已经算一首诗了。
